title: Wine Wimsey Review · Wed Nov 4
subtitle: 16 feed posts (15 images + 1 TOBI at #8) and 4 stories. TOBIs: ISO week 45 is odd, so Wednesday gets 1. Posting date is Wed Nov 4 (next unused folder); if you meant Nov 5, say so. Inbox 0 new, held 0. All character posts are The Hot Mess; #9 is a people-free still life with the AI label. Flags: #3 and #10 were regenerated once to fix the stamp over the bottom text and the WineWimsey stamp still sits on the last words of the bottom strip on both (cropping or a retry needed); #6 has a double space in the image text.

posts.quote: MY HAIRDRESSER ASKED WHAT I WANTED DONE. I SAID FEWER GREY HAIRS AND MORE PATIENCE. SHE SAID SHE ONLY DOES HAIR.
posts.caption: She has been cutting my hair for nine years and has never once fallen for this line. I arrive with magazine photos and optimism. She studies both, picks up the scissors, and says "there, that's you." The cape goes into the hamper, I check the mirror from two angles, and I tip more than I should. It's a fair price for being told the truth by someone holding scissors.
posts.first: There is a grey patch above my left ear that she calls character. I would prefer a refund. I've decided to take it personally for the rest of October, privately, with a small grudge and a decent haircut.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun and glasses on her forehead sitting in a salon chair beside a station with a glass of wine, talking to a hairdresser. Text at the top reads: My hairdresser asked what I wanted done. I said fewer grey hairs and more patience. She said she only does hair.

posts.quote: I BOUGHT A STEP COUNTER. IT CONGRATULATED ME FOR WALKING TO THE MAILBOX. I ACCEPTED THE CREDIT.
posts.caption: It buzzed at 2:40 with tiny fireworks after eleven steps to the end of the driveway. I took the compliment and kept walking.
posts.first: It saves its praise for the first trip of the day, like a bakery with one fresh batch. I've adjusted my schedule around the mailbox accordingly. It's the best coaching I've had in years.
posts.alt: Comic-panel cartoon of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun and glasses on her forehead holding a wrist step counter that shows fireworks after a short walk to a mailbox. Text at the top reads: I bought a step counter. It congratulated me for walking to the mailbox. I accepted the credit.

posts.quote: THE NEIGHBOR'S LEAF BLOWER STARTED AT 8 A.M. ON SATURDAY. I RESPONDED BY SITTING DOWN AND REFUSING TO BE PRODUCTIVE IN FRONT OF IT.
posts.caption: He starts at eight sharp, every weekend, like a man with a deadline and a grudge. I dragged the porch chair to the front like a picket line and took my coffee with me. By ten he had moved four piles of leaves twelve feet to the left. I held my position and said nothing, which is my strongest form of protest. The leaves, I noticed, did not say anything either.
posts.first: His yard is the cleanest on the street. Mine had a blanket, a mug, and a small crowd of squirrels who agreed with me. He has an extension cord. I had a plan. We both feel good about our weekends.
posts.alt: Illustrated scene of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun and glasses on her forehead sitting in a porch chair holding a coffee mug with arms crossed, while a neighbor blows autumn leaves across the fence. Text at the top reads: The neighbor's leaf blower started at 8 a.m. on Saturday. Text at the bottom reads: I responded by sitting down and refusing to be productive in front of it.

posts.quote: I BROUGHT A COUPON AND THE CASHIER ASKED FOR MY PHONE. IT'S A PAPER COUPON, BRENDA. IT HAS SCISSOR MARKS.
posts.caption: I cut it out of the Sunday paper on Saturday with the good scissors. The cashier turned it over twice, then looked at me like I'd handed her a telegram. We studied it together for a while. It was a quiet, shared moment.
posts.first: In the end she typed the numbers in by hand. I saved forty cents, it cost her four minutes, and she handed the coupon back to me still cut and crooked. I put it in my purse. It will have another life.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun and glasses on her forehead at a grocery checkout holding up a paper coupon toward a puzzled cashier, a glass of wine beside the register. Text in the speech bubble reads: I brought a coupon and the cashier asked for my phone. It's a paper coupon, Brenda. It has scissor marks.

posts.quote: My voicemail greeting is eleven years old. People still say it sounds like me. I tell them she's doing great.
posts.caption: I recorded it in a hallway in 2015 on a phone I no longer own. She sounds rested and a little too cheerful about returning calls. My sister calls her the old me. I keep meaning to re-record it, but she has such confidence. I'd hate to let her go before she's heard from a few more people.
posts.first: A warranty caller left the only voicemail I've had since August. He hung up in the middle of her pause. She kept her composure, and I admire that more every year.
posts.alt: Character card illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun and glasses on her forehead holding a smartphone and a glass of wine, looking fondly at the screen. Text on the card reads: My voicemail greeting is eleven years old. People still say it sounds like me. I tell them she's doing great.

posts.quote: I LIFTED A BAG OF POTTING SOIL  LIKE IT WAS 1998. MY LOWER BACK HAS STARTED A FILE.
posts.caption: The bag said forty pounds. I thought about 1998 and picked it up anyway. Then I stood perfectly still for a full minute while my back reviewed my choices. I repotted the geranium very slowly, lowering each scoop like a crane operator on a union break. The geranium is thriving. I'm making notes.
posts.first: The neighbor waved from her driveway and I held my spine with the other hand and waved back. By evening there was a heating pad on my porch rail with no note. I never found out who she was. I sat on it right away.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun and glasses on her forehead stooping beside a large bag of potting soil in a garden with a wine glass on a ledge, a hand on her lower back. Text in the speech bubble reads: I lifted a bag of potting soil like it was 1998. My lower back has started a file.

posts.quote: I WENT TO THREE STORES FOR ONE PAIR OF BLACK PANTS. THE PANTS DON'T EXIST. NEITHER DOES MY PATIENCE FOR DRESSING ROOMS.
posts.caption: Store one had only grey. Store two had a size from a different decade. Store three's dressing room curtain didn't close, and I decided that was the universe's final word.
posts.first: Later I found a pair of black pants in the back of my own closet. They have always fit. I wore them Thursday and felt a little silly about the whole trip. The receipts for gas say otherwise.
posts.alt: Comic-panel cartoon of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun and glasses on her forehead holding a pile of clothes in a store dressing room with a curtain that won't close, a wine glass on the bench. Text at the top reads: I went to three stores for one pair of black pants. The pants don't exist. Neither does my patience for dressing rooms.

posts.quote: I used to want a big life. Now I want a parking spot near the entrance and a quiet checkout line.
posts.first: Last Tuesday I parked far from the door anyway, because I had the time. The checkout line was short. A man held the door and said have a good one. It was a perfect errand. I sat in the car for a minute afterward to let it sink in.

posts.quote: I STOOD UP FROM THE COUCH AND MY KNEES APPLAUDED. STANDING OVATION, NO ENCORE.
posts.caption: First the creak, then the pop, and I swear there was sound design. The cat didn't look over. She has seen this performance before and gave it no stars. The kitchen has a lovely echo, though, so I stood there a moment and let the applause carry. A woman needs a small audience now and then.
posts.first: I stood up during a phone call and my friend asked if I was eating something. I said no, that was just me. We spent the next twenty minutes comparing hips and agreed to stay in touch.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun and glasses on her forehead getting up from a couch with a wine glass in hand and an amused grimace, a cat looking away. Text in the speech bubble reads: I stood up from the couch and my knees applauded. Standing ovation, no encore.

posts.quote: The rain started at noon and so did my afternoon plans, which are to watch it.
posts.caption: It was dry at breakfast. By noon the sky changed its mind, and I took it as a sign to cancel everything I'd never planned.
posts.first: I had the cheese plate ready before the rain warmed up. The candle burned down an inch and the window fogged at the edges. That was the entire point, and it worked.
posts.alt: Still life photo of a rain-streaked window with a glass of red wine, a lit candle and a small cheese plate on a table. Text at the top reads: The rain started at noon and so did my afternoon plans, which are to watch it.

posts.quote: I TURNED OFF THE NEWS AND WATCHED A MAN RESTORE A RUSTY WHEELBARROW FOR FORTY MINUTES. MY SHOULDERS CAME DOWN TWO INCHES.
posts.caption: He wore a flat cap and spoke to the wheelbarrow in the voice of a man who has all the time there is. Six episodes about a shed followed. I only meant to watch one. By the end I was sitting differently, and the dog was asleep on my feet. It turns out calm is just somebody else's patience on a screen.
posts.first: He found a number stamped under the rust and said, well, look at that. I paused the show, made tea, and thought about that number for a while. Nothing in the news has done that for me lately.
posts.alt: Illustrated scene of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun and glasses on her forehead relaxing in an armchair with a glass of wine while a television shows a man restoring a rusty wheelbarrow in a barn, a dog asleep beside her. Text at the top reads: I turned off the news and watched a man restore a rusty wheelbarrow for forty minutes. Text at the bottom reads: My shoulders came down two inches.

posts.quote: THE DISHWASHER HAS MORE SETTINGS THAN MY CAR. I USE THE ONE THAT'S ALREADY LIT.
posts.caption: The manual is a hundred pages and has never been opened. One button lights up, and that's the one for me.
posts.first: A friend suggested eco mode last month. I looked it up and found I had been using it by accident for three years. I've decided to call that a lifestyle.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun and glasses on her forehead standing at a dishwasher with many buttons, one glowing, a glass of wine on the counter. Text in the speech bubble reads: The dishwasher has more settings than my car. I use the one that's already lit.

posts.quote: I FOUND A RECEIPT FROM 2013 IN A COAT POCKET. THE PIZZA WAS $11. I THOUGHT ABOUT THAT FOR A LONG TIME.
posts.caption: Two slices, a salad nobody finished, a soda, and a tip written in blue pen. I stood in the hallway trying to remember who I was with and which night it was. I got nowhere. The receipt faded at the edges like it was embarrassed for me. I still kept it, in case it comes back to me.
posts.first: The other pocket had a concert ticket stub I also don't remember. That coat has a better social calendar than I do. I hung it back up with some respect.
posts.alt: Comic-panel cartoon of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun and glasses on her forehead holding a small paper receipt up to the light beside a coat on a hook, a wine glass in the other hand. Text at the top reads: I found a receipt from 2013 in a coat pocket. The pizza was $11. I thought about that for a long time.

posts.quote: 'Because I said so' was my mother's whole legal argument. It still wins every case in my house.
posts.caption: She used it for bedtimes, vegetables, and the radio station in the car. I told the dog to get off the couch with it and he obeyed.
posts.first: He got down slowly and looked back at me the whole way. I understood my mother a little better right then. Ten minutes later I let him back up, and nobody mentioned the ruling.
posts.alt: Character card illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun and glasses on her forehead standing with a wine glass and one finger raised, a dog looking up from a couch behind her. Text on the card reads: 'Because I said so' was my mother's whole legal argument. It still wins every case in my house.

posts.quote: AT TWENTY I STAYED UP ALL NIGHT FOR A BAND. AT FIFTY-TWO I STAY UP ALL NIGHT BECAUSE OF ONE SLICE OF PIZZA.
posts.caption: I had one small slice at 8:30 with the confidence of a 2 a.m. pizza person. At midnight I was propped on three pillows in a seated position my grandmother would have approved of. The ceiling and I had a long talk. It had no advice, which I respected. Dinner has become a matter of strategy and timing. Nobody sent me the playbook.
posts.first: I've started setting out water, a chewable, and a sticky note on the pizza box. It says think about 3 a.m. I read it, nod, and have the second slice anyway.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun and glasses on her forehead sitting up in bed on three pillows with a wine glass on the nightstand and a pizza box nearby, wide awake. Text in the speech bubble reads: At twenty I stayed up all night for a band. At fifty-two I stay up all night because of one slice of pizza.

posts.quote: I BOUGHT NEXT YEAR'S PLANNER IN NOVEMBER. IT'S THE ONLY TIME I TRUST MYSELF COMPLETELY.
posts.caption: It's green, cloth-covered, and has a ribbon. On page two I wrote three goals in my best handwriting. By January I'll have moved two of them to page nine, where goals go to rest. The planner is smooth and blank and hopeful. We'll both be fine until about the second week of March.
posts.first: I use four pen colors. Blue for appointments, green for ideas, and red for things I'm avoiding. By February it's all the same color, and the planner and I just carry on.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun and glasses on her forehead at a desk holding a new green cloth-covered planner with a ribbon, a pen behind her ear and a glass of wine beside it. Text in the speech bubble reads: I bought next year's planner in November. It's the only time I trust myself completely.

stories.quote: PAID FOR PARKING WITH A COIN I FOUND IN MY COAT. WINNING ISN'T LOUD AT MY AGE.
stories.alt: Comic-panel cartoon of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun and glasses on her forehead dropping a found coin into a parking meter with a quiet smile. Text at the top reads: Paid for parking with a coin I found in my coat. Winning isn't loud at my age.

stories.quote: MY PHONE AUTOCORRECTED MY OWN NAME TODAY. WE'RE NO LONGER ON SPEAKING TERMS.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun and glasses on her forehead glaring at her phone held at arm's length. Text in the speech bubble reads: My phone autocorrected my own name today. We're no longer on speaking terms.

stories.quote: I STOOD IN THE PRODUCE AISLE FOR TEN MINUTES DECIDING BETWEEN TWO IDENTICAL LEMONS. I CHOSE THE LEFT.
stories.alt: Illustrated scene of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun and glasses on her forehead standing in a produce aisle holding two lemons, comparing them. Text at the top reads: I stood in the produce aisle for ten minutes deciding between two identical lemons. Text at the bottom reads: I chose the left.

stories.quote: Went to bed at nine. Woke at nine-fifteen thinking it was morning. Won't be discussing it.
stories.alt: Character card illustration of a woman with a messy grey-streaked bun and glasses on her forehead sitting up in bed looking at a bedside clock in the dark. Text on the card reads: Went to bed at nine. Woke at nine-fifteen thinking it was morning. Won't be discussing it.
